items.statement: FY26 sanction guidance of INR60,000 crores, with INR25,000 crores already sanctioned
items.quote: we have targeted around INR30,000 crores for disbursement and around INR60,000 crores for sanction of the assets.

items.statement: AUM expected to cross INR5 lakh crores in FY27
items.quote: sometime in FY '27, we should cross INR5 lakh mark of our asset under management for this company.

items.statement: NIM improved to 1.51% in Q1 FY26 from 1.31% in previous quarter
items.quote: So you see NIM that we have come out for this quarter is 1.51 which is quite above what we showed last quarter that was nearly 1.31.

items.statement: New business margins expected to exceed 2%
items.quote: for the additional asset that we are entering into our system, the NIM will be more than 2%.

items.statement: Margins on new assets 2-3x higher than those from Indian Railways
items.quote: My margins are 2 to 3x of what I used to get from Indian Railways.

items.statement: Spreads on refinancing loans range from 100-150 bps
items.quote: Rate differential is minimum 100 bps. At times, it is 150 bps also.

items.statement: Spreads on metro projects expected to be 30-35 bps
items.quote: metro railway is something is the nation service. And with my robust balance sheet, with my low overhead cost, if I'm making 30-35 bps out of that, it's very good.

items.statement: Spreads on new assets range from 70-150 bps
items.quote: It would be in the range of 70 bps to 150 bps, what we are charging from various customers.

items.statement: Cost of capital around 7% (actual cost, excluding capitalized interest)
items.quote: So far as cost of capital is concerned, yes, it is hovering around 7%.

items.statement: High demand for IRFC's funding from CPSEs, state governments, and metro railways
items.quote: We are really excited to have those kind s of queries. In fact, the team is working overtime with a kind of inflow of the customers

items.statement: Zero NPA commitment maintained through government-linked assets and strict due diligence
items.quote: we are very particular about the quality of the assets. As you know, we are perhaps the only zero NPA company and we wish to remain that.

items.statement: Overhead costs to remain below 0.2% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: we don't foresee our overhead cost going even 0.2% in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: No corporate tax liability expected for next 5-7 years due to unabsorbed depreciation
items.quote: we have a lot of unabsorbed depreciation that will be going forward also for a foreseeable future of 5 to 7 years, that will be sufficient to absorb whatever income we have.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost guidance of 1.2% (including CGFMU premium) and steady-state 1%
items.quote: So for this particular year, we will look to have a credit cost of around 1.2 one quarter. On a steady-state basis, we will be having credit costs just about near about 1%.

items.statement: FY26 GNPA guidance of 5% and NNPA of 3% (before CGFMU claims)
items.quote: Overall, I think we have guided for 5 and 3. But of course, the timing of the CGFMU play is a critical thing. So it may be. But what would be is that, by and large, we'll try to maintain the NNPA minus the CGFMU cover, very close to 0%.

items.statement: NIMs expected at 7.5-8% with 55-45 secured-unsecured mix
items.quote: We expect the NIMs to be in the region of 7.5% to 8% with the mix that we have. We shall continue to maintain this mix of 55%, 45% between secured and unsecured.

items.statement: CGFMU claims to reduce headline GNPA in Q3 FY26
items.quote: So our expectation is that the claim will be fulfilled in third quarter. So we do see a reduction in the headline GNPA number by the time we report Q3.

items.statement: Slippages to reduce ₹50-70 cr in Q2 FY26 vs Q1 FY26 (₹278 cr)
items.quote: Yes. Yes. We certainly expect that. So we would want that our slippages reduces anywhere between ₹50 crore to ₹70 crore in the next quarter.

items.statement: NPA accretion to stabilize by Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: So hopefully, if this trend continues, then it's near back to normalcy in Q3 and probably in Q4.

items.statement: CV portfolio grew >50% YoY, mortgage >30% YoY
items.quote: CV on a year-on-year basis has grown more than 50%. Mortgage has grown more than 30%.

items.statement: Secured portfolio (CV + mortgage) to drive growth vs inclusive finance
items.quote: Given the base that we have in both these businesses, our growth will continue to be quite high relative to what we plan to do in IF.

items.statement: IF portfolio shifted to individual loans (2/3 of total IF)
items.quote: Our individual loans are actually become now two third of our overall IF portfolio.

items.statement: IF disbursals returned to Q1 FY25 levels
items.quote: We have gone back to the more or less same disbursal numbers of Q1 FY25 as this quarter.

items.statement: Credit cost upfronted at 27% for non-CGFMU slippages (73% claimable)
items.quote: We provide the entire amount, which is not claimable under CGMFU is approximately 23%. We don't provide 25% of 23%. We provide the entire 27% in the same quarter, 73% is claimable.

items.statement: IF collection efficiency improved to 98.4% (June '25) and 99.5% (last 6 months)
items.quote: Current bucket collection efficiency increased from 97.5% in April '25 to 98.4% in June '25, and the current bucket collection efficiency of the last 6 months of portfolio is at 99.5%.

items.statement: IF GNPA at 8.5% (₹918 cr), NNPA at 5.6% (₹593 cr) with ₹584 cr CGFMU cover
items.quote: Our current GNPA is at 8.5% as of June 2025, and NNPA is at 5.6%. GNPA stood at ₹918 crore and NNPA at ₹593 crore, against which ₹584 crore is receivable under the CGFMU scheme.

items.statement: IF slippages ₹240 cr (of ₹280 cr total) in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Out of the ₹280 crore of slippages that we have at the bank level, ₹240 crore is on account of microfinance.

items.statement: IF portfolio >98% covered under CGFMU
items.quote: More than 98% of the portfolio is now covered under the scheme.

name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.quote: we have Large Cap Fund, Flexi-Cap Fund and Multi-Asset Allocation Fund, Balanced Advantage Fund and GenNext funds. ... These are the 5 focused products that we kept

items.quote: We thought let us focus on reviving the performance on these funds with respect to the competition. And then when the time comes right, we'll start pushing these funds

items.statement: No distributor commission cuts planned; maintaining margins for scale-building
items.quote: we don't want to take the call at this time given the need of the business to grow the business, the next level of growth and build scale

items.statement: Offshore assets at ₹10,588 crores; GIFT City fundraising for ESG, Flexi Cap, Global Blue-Chip funds
items.quote: Our offshore assets stood at about INR10,588 crores for Q1 FY26. Under the GIFT City platform, we have a fundraising underway for the India ESG Engagement Fund, ABSL Flexi Cap Fund

items.statement: KFC SSSG to turn positive soon, driven by value campaigns and consumer base expansion
items.quote: I am quite confident on KFC that we should be able to start changing this soon. What are we focusing on? We are focusing on really at a consumer level there are two consumers. We believe that the biggest opportunity for KFC is increasing the consuming base for KFC

items.statement: Pizza Hut pan-India rollout of Tamil Nadu strategy expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: I am sure it's only a matter of quarter or two before all the three parties are on the same page and we can execute uniformly pan India.

items.statement: Sri Lanka margins to improve slightly QoQ from Q2FY26 due to price hikes
items.quote: we expect at least Q 2FY26 we should be able to deliver slightly better improvement over margins QoQ at least

items.statement: KFC gross margins flexible; willing to sacrifice margins for transaction growth
items.quote: we would be a bit more flexible on those gross margin numbers if it can eventually result into a higher transaction growth and higher SSSG.

items.statement: KFC to launch more value campaigns (e.g., 100-rupee offers) in H2 FY26
items.quote: in H2, you will see even more campaign on some 100 rupees as well.

items.statement: KFC delivery mix to remain range-bound (~43%) for FY26
items.quote: we would say that it should largely be range bound in terms of the delivery mix.

items.statement: KFC margins bottomed out at current SSSG levels (flat), seasonal impacts only
items.quote: at these SSSG levels which is a flat SSSG levels there should only be now seasonal impacts which should play out.

items.quote: SSSG which was flat over last year. However, transaction growth was positive, which is encour aging, and transaction growth was positive because gross margin also was negative

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG 12%, system growth 15%
items.quote: Sri Lanka continued to show robust double-digit SSSG and SSTG. In fact, SSSG came in at 12% and system growth was 15%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA margin 12.7% (30 bps higher YoY, offset by wage hikes)
items.quote: Overall restaurant EBITDA came in at 12.7%. And as Sanjay called out, we couldn't really see the margin expansion because the benefit of SSSG was largely offset by the increase in minimum wages.

items.statement: Sri Lanka took 3-5% price hike to mitigate wage inflation impact
items.quote: we have taken a price increase of 3 %-5% in Sri Lanka and we expect at least Q 2FY26 we should be able to deliver slightly better improvement over margins QoQ

items.statement: KFC delivery mix increased 300 bps YoY (43% in Q1 FY26)
items.quote: Delivery mix while it was similar to the previous quarter, but if you look at year-on-year, there is a 300 basis points increase in delivery mix.

items.statement: KFC dine-in growth slower than delivery; value campaigns to bridge gap
items.quote: The Epic Saver and the promotions and those campaigns definitely has helped us reduce the gap between the dine-in performance and delivery performance.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance updated to INR 675-700 crore (earlier INR 650-700 crore)
items.quote: So, it appears INR 675 crores to INR 700 crores seems to be a very good possibility because already we are at a INR 150 crores run rate.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin guidance maintained at ~16-16.5%
items.quote: we feel we will be able to maintain this around this margin, 16%, 16.5% PAT margin.

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance provided; focus on R&D and talent investment
items.quote: We remain committed to strengthening our innovation pipeline and enhancing our go-to-market capabilities.

items.statement: Enterprise Solutions order book grew 28% YoY
items.quote: The order book you asked. So order book, Enterprise order book has grown by 28%.

items.statement: Shift toward higher-margin software products (80-85% gross margin) in Enterprise Solutions India
items.quote: Today, we reduced the hardware and mainly focusing on software so that we are able to get around 80%, 85% gross margin on the enterprise software product business.

items.statement: U.S. service business growth muted due to visa restrictions (H1, L1) and operational challenges
items.quote: the growth in the service side may be muted because the AI is coming and then the lot of visa kind of restrictions are there, H1 visa rest riction, L1 visa

items.statement: Geographic revenue split: U.S. (INR 60 crore), Middle East/Africa (INR 35 crore), India (INR 55 crore), Asia Pacific (INR 4-6 crore)

items.quote: I think maybe around INR 60 crores come from USA; and around Middle East, Africa will be INR 34 crores, INR 35 crores; balance about INR 55 crores will be India, roughly.

items.statement: Average deal size in Enterprise Solutions increased to INR 10-20 crore (from INR 4-5 crore earlier)
items.quote: earlier days, we were bidding INR 4 crores, INR 5 crores kind of deal, but now quite a bit of deals are in the range of INR 10 crores to INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin to stay at current levels (~35%) for next 9 months unless major oil disruption
items.quote: Currently, we are at close to 35% gross margin at console level. But overall, at standalone level also, we are at highest gross margin. And we see that in next nine months also, we'll be at the same, we'll be maintaining the same gross margin, what we see right now. Unless, we see any major disruption in oil, edible oil also.

items.statement: Volume growth to reach 9-10% for FY26, with sequential improvement from Q2
items.quote: So, we've seen good demand recovery across month -on-month. So, for rest of the year, we see at least 9%, 10% volume growth. That's the plan. And that's the numbers , we are looking at, at least

items.quote: So, on full year basis, what we see that on a stand alone basis, stand alone basis you see gross margin of 32% plus. That's the target what we're taking on stand alone basis without PLI. And we are on track of it this year, of doing the same.

items.statement: Nepal JV to reach INR 50 Cr top line in next 2 years
items.quote: And we see a good potential, as brand is very strong there. But overall, due to custom duty and all, we're not able to supply in Nepal market. We see good potential coming up and using and driving distribution of CG Group Wai Wai, and we see at least INR 50 Crores top line in the next two years. That's the target what we see.

items.statement: Direct outlet coverage to reach 5 Lakh by FY29 (from 3.26 Lakh currently)
items.quote: The target what we have is to exceed 3.5 Lakh outlets by end of the year. But year-on-year is what we shall be adding 50,000 outlets. That's what is the target, what we have for ourselves and should reach to 5,00,000 outlets in our direct coverage. That's the target what we have in the next 3 years.

items.statement: PLI of INR 50 Cr factored for FY26 (INR 12.5 Cr per quarter)
items.quote: So, for FY '26, we have factored close to INR 50 Crores PLI in our books. So, it will divide equal in each quarter.

items.statement: Family packs grew 15.8% vs. 8.2% for impulse packs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In the last quarter, our family packs have grown by far higher than the impulse packs, which is INR 5 and INR 10 per pack. So, the family pack has delivered a 15.8% growth, whereas impulse packs are at 8.2%.

items.statement: Ethnic snacks grew 11.2%, packaged sweets 3.1%, Western snacks 4.2%, papad 5.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In ethnic snacks, which is our core category, has grown at 11.2%. Packaged sweets, which looks pretty low at this point, is at 3.1%, but this is a seasonal business. This is going to be recovered in quarter 2. Western snacks are also showing a 4.2% revenue growth, and papad, a small category, is growing slowly at 5.8%.

items.statement: Exports grew 60.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Exports have done extremely well with a 60.8% market revenue growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at ~14.8% (consolidated) and ~15.8% (standalone) in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA from a consolidated basis, we had touched an EBITDA close to 14.8% and without PLI 13%. So, close to 15% EBITDA with PLI. And from a stand alone basis also, we are just close to 15.8% EBITDA with PLI and close to 13.5% EBITDA without PLI.

items.statement: Prices increased by 2.5% in last 2-2.5 quarters to regain margins
items.quote: On timely basis, also, we’ve increased the prices of key ethnic snacks as well as special snacks. So, in the last 2, 2.5 quarters, we have increased prices by 2.5%. That has also helped us in regaining our margin trend.

items.statement: Raw material costs (pulses, edible oils) softened due to good crop and rain, aiding margins
items.quote: Also, this year, we have seen good rain, a good crop, and raw materials supported as key pulses edible have also softened. So, this is also playing an instrumental role in improving gross margin.

items.statement: Rural and urban demand improved sequentially in Q1 FY26
items.quote: From the last 6, 7 months, we've seen good demand improvement across each month-on-month. So, if you see the third quarter of last year, we have been at 5%, 6% growth versus last quarter was good. And this quarter, month-on-month basis, we've seen good demand recovery across each rural as well as urban.

items.statement: Core markets grew 8.5%, focus markets 11.5%, other markets 26.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The way we look at our business, which is core focus in other markets. So, core has grown at 8.5%; focus market at 11.5%; and other markets is at 26.5% growth.

items.statement: Revenue and profit growth in FY27 with doubled cell/module capacity and new revenue streams (BESS, inverters, wafers)
items.quote: FY27 will be a pivotal year for Premier Energies. We'll be more than doubling our cell and module capacities and unlocking new revenues across different streams like BESS, inverters, inverter, and wafer.

items.statement: Accelerated capex for BESS and inverter lines to start contributing in Q1 FY27; 4.8 GW cell/module and wafer capacity in Q1-Q2 FY27
items.quote: We have accelerated our BSS and inverter lines, which will now come in Q1 of FY27, and our wafer manufacturing, our 4.8 gigawatt cell and module, all that is available in the presentation. Most of them are coming up in Q1 FY27, and I think something in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: US policy/tariff uncertainty; no impact on Indian market (export reliance <1%)
items.quote: we have decided to continue keeping those plans on hold for now, pending greater clarity on the U.S. policy and tariffs. items.statement: No explicit fund-raising guidance; capex funded via internal cash flow and debt
items.quote: All projects are progressing well, both on timelines and within budget, reflecting our disciplined execution and long-term vision.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for FY27; no specific numbers disclosed
items.quote: we have a very strong pipeline going into FY '27. The number is fairly large, but we generally refrain from, giving numbers as a future guidance

items.statement: US anti-dumping duty unlikely to impact; Indian market insulated due to low export reliance
items.quote: Our reliance on the export market is next to nil. And hence we are protected irrespective of the outcome of this investigation.

items.statement: IPPs locking orders due to rising prices; strong demand for DCR modules
items.quote: We are seeing a strong uptake of IPPs wanting to close quickly now and, this will of course show up in our next quarterly results

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth of 50% and PAT growth of 100% over FY25
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering 50% growth in top line and about 100% growth in PAT for FY26 over FY25.

items.statement: US regulated market revenue of ~₹400 crore in FY26
items.quote: So, this year from our US regulated side, we expect to do about INR 400 odd crores.

items.statement: US regulated market revenue CAGR of 20-30% post-FY26
items.quote: And on a steady state going forward basis, you can assume between 20% to 30% CAGR growth, you know. That's what we anticipate and that's what we feel we'll be able to achieve.

items.statement: CDMO-CMO revenue of ~₹200 crore in FY26 (50% of US revenue)
items.quote: That's our this year projection. Going forward, as I said, about 20%, 30% CAGR growth is what we expect out of our U.S. side of the business. So, typically, if we keep the same split on the business, that will give us that kind of visibility on the CDMO-CMO side of the

items.statement: Emerging market EBITDA margin to stabilize at 15-17% annually

items.statement: Emerging market EBITDA margin to reach 10% in FY26
items.quote: We believe we should reach closer to double-digit, hopefully. At least around 10% is what we are believing.

items.statement: Emerging market EBITDA margin to reach mid-teens in FY27
items.quote: So, I think 100% next year, we should be in mid-teens in the emerging market in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Branded generics revenue of ₹50 crore in FY26
items.quote: The branded generics business is expected to surpass revenue of INR 50 crores in FY26.

items.statement: US manufacturing capacity to increase from 1.2B to 2B units by FY26 end
items.quote: This expansion will take the overall capacity at our US manufacturing plant from 1.2 billion units to almost 2 billion units.

items.statement: FDA approval for new API facility expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: I think what we said is Q2 next year is when we expect FDA to come and inspect.

items.statement: 15-16 ANDA products to be launched in FY26 (majority in H2)

items.quote: There could be some regulatory risk, there could be some foreseeable risk that we already know, right? We don't foresee any, or maybe some outrageous discussion on the tariffs, right, which we don't anticipate, but you never know.

items.quote: Regulated markets are expected to continue contributing around 60%-70% of total revenue, with emerging markets continuing to account for about 30%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 35%-40%

items.statement: New orders expected in Q2-Q3 FY26 for aero tooling and precision segments
items.quote: I'm expecting a large order inflows to come in in Q2 and Q3, both in aero tooling as well as precision segment.

items.statement: New high-value engine stands order, production starts Q2 FY26, deliveries Q3-Q4 FY26
items.quote: We secured a new order for a high-value engine stands. Production will begin in this quarter, that is Q2, with deliveries expected in Q3 and early Q4.

items.quote: anticipating rise in direct drop shipments to end customers' premises to minimize tariff impact for non-U.S. goods. I will try to indicate maybe about 70% of our goods to end customers are based outside U.S

items.quote: In the first Unimech Aerospace and quarter of FY26, the momentum continued of receiving strong business inquiries from both domestic and international customers. We added around three new customers during the quarter

items.quote: This might involve some kind of funding -- debt funding related to be required for which I have already factored additional data around INR50 crores ready, but not yet availed.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% despite Q1 outperformance
items.quote: So, therefore, we still stick to overall guidance of 15% for the year. Pharma industry, as we are all aware, is not growing as fast as it used to in the past. So, I think we are not upping our guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 100-150 bps maintained for FY26

items.statement: ROE expected to remain in 18%-19% range for next 2 years

items.quote: No. So, we are selling thin on that product. We are not competing as much as we should have been. So, that product has come down considerably.
